la:noun:fax.html:
fax, făcis (also in the
nom. sing. † faces, acc. to Paul. ex Müll.; gen. plur.: facum, acc. to P., but without example), f.
root bhā, to shine; cf. favilla
, a torch, firebrand, flambeau, link, orig. of pine or other resinous wood.
Lit. (syn.: taeda, funale, cerĕus, candela, lucerna, laterna): alii faces atque aridam materiem de muro in aggerem eminus jaciebant, * ; : ambulare cum facibus,: malleolos et faces ad inflammandam urbem comparare,; cf.: ego faces jam accensas ad hujus urbis incendium exstinxi,: servi in tecta nostra cum facibus immissi,; cf.: faces incendere,: si te in Capitolium faces ferre vellet,: ardentem facem praeferre,: castris inicere,; subdere urbi,: faces ferro inspicare,; cf.: facis incidere,: dilapsam in cineres facem,.—At weddings, the torch carried before the bride on the way to her home, usually made of white-thorn (Spina alba) or pine, the nuptial torch: spina, nuptiarum facibus auspicatissima, Masur. ap. ; Fest. s. v. patrimi, p. 245; s. v. rapi, p. 289 Müll.; Varr. ap. ; id. ap. ; ; ; ; ; ; hence, nuptiales,; : maritae,: legitimae,.—Cf. Anthon's Dict. of Antiq. p. 434, and v.infra. Torches were also carried in funeral processions, ; (4, 12), 17; ; ; ; id. Vit. Beat. fin.; ; and in the Eleusinian mysteries,.—An attribute of Cupid, ; (4, 15), 16; ; ; of the Furies,; ; ; ; —
Transf.
On account of the use of torches at weddings (poet.), a wedding, marriage: face nuptiali digna,; cf.: te face sollemni junget sibi,.—And referring at the same time to the funeral torch: viximus insignes inter utramque facem,i. e. between marriage and death,—
The light of the heavenly bodies (poet.): dum roseā face sol inferret lumina caelo,; cf.: Phoebi fax, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 11, 18: canentes Rite crescentem face Noctilucam,: aeterna fax,i. e. the sun,.—
A fiery meteor, fire-ball, shooting-star, comet: noctivagaeque faces caeli flammaeque volantes,; cf.: nocturnasque faces caeli, sublime volantes,: emicant et faces non nisi cum decidunt visae, etc.,: tum facibus visis caelestibus, tum stellis iis, quas Graeci cometas, nostri cincinnatas vocant,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; .—
Of lightning: facem flammantem dirigere,; . —
Of the eyes: oculi, geminae, sidera nostra, faces,: has ego credo faces, haec virginis ora Dianae,; cf.: tranquillaeque faces oculis et plurima vultu materinest,.—
Prima fax (noctis), early torchlight, immediately after dark (post-class.); cf.: luminibus accensis, Auct. B. Afr. 89: tempus diei occiduum, mox suprema tempestas, hoc est diei novissimum tempus: deinde vespera: ab hoc tempore prima fax dicitur, deinde concubia, etc.,; ; fin.; .
Trop.
That which illuminates, makes conspicuous (poet.): incipit parentum nobilitas facem praeferre pudendis,; cf. .—
That which inflames or incites, incitement, stimulus, cause of ruin, destruction (freq. and class.): cum corporis facibus inflammari soleamus ad omnes fere cupiditates eoque magis incendi, quod, etc.,: me torret face mutua Calais,flame of love,; cf.: iraï fax,: dicendi faces,flames, fires of eloquence,; cf.: alicui quasi quasdam verborum faces admovere,: alicui acriores ad studia dicendi faces subdere, Spald.: hortator studii causaque faxque mei,guide, leader,; and: incitator et fax omnium, Prud. στεφ. 10, 67: subicere faces invidiae alicujus,; cf.: flagrantibus jam militum animis velut faces addere,: acerrimam bello facem praetulit,: (rogationes promulgavit) duas faces novantibus res ad plebem in optimates accendendam,: inde faces ardent, a dote,: adolescentulo ad libidinem facem praeferre, i. e. to be a leader or guide, : Antonius omnium Clodi incendiorum fax,instigator,; cf.: fax accusationis et origo,: fax hujus belli (Hannibal),; : dolorum cum admoventur faces,; cf. : (dolor) ardentes faces intentat,: quae (Agrippinae) Gaium et Domitium Neronem principes genuere totidem facis generis humani,destroyers,.—Absol.: cum his furiis et facibus, cum his exitiosis prodigiis (i e. Gabinio et Pisone),.
